LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we write a paragraph?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts of a paragraph for information
2. write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.3.1 WRITING FOR INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify parts of a paragraph for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of a paragraph for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of a paragraph for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of a paragraph for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression

What this means
In this part you learn to write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify parts of a paragraph for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information to a partner. (skill: write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of a paragraph for information.
3. Practise this skill: write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we write a paragraph?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.3.1 Writing for information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of a paragraph for information.
5. Be able to: write a short coherent paragraph on the theme for self-expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
